targets.text: eidetic recall gains an opt-in reranker stage: --rerank re-scores the primary hits with the lobes cross-encoder and exposes rerank_score beside score, and the reranker's fallback to lexical overlap is never silent again

the whole feature is exercised by hermetic tests with an injected client - no test reaches a live lane - AND at least one live run against the real lobes gateway reproduces the issue table (on-topic records kept, distractor dropped) before the PR merges

eidetic/memory/embed.py already ships the whole remote lane: rerank() -> _remote_rerank() POSTs {base_url}/rerank with _rerank_model and parses results[].relevance_score (falling back to results[].score); the change wires an existing method into recall, it does not build a client
the shipped rerank()/_remote_rerank() is called as-is: if wiring it requires changing its request or response parsing, that is a separate finding to state, not a silent edit folded into this change

the rerank stage lands in eidetic/cli/_commands/recall.py's cmd_recall, between the lifecycle filter and the top-k slice: today the code fetches ALL ranked hits (top_k=2**31), lifecycle-filters, then slices [:top_k], so a rerank pass has a natural candidate pool wider than top-k already in hand
the rerank pass is proven to sit AFTER the lifecycle filter: a test shows a shadowed or archived record is never sent to the reranker, so lifecycle filtering is never bypassed by the new stage

Record (eidetic/memory/record.py) gains a recall-only rerank_score field alongside score and signal, threaded through to_dict/from_dict, AND added to the set cmd_recall clears on the reinforcement copy (bumped.score = None; bumped.signal = None) so a query-time number is never persisted
a round-trip test proves rerank_score never persists: after a --rerank recall, re-reading the reinforced records from the store shows rerank_score absent/None, exactly as score and signal already are

recall.py holds no EmbedClient today - StoreBackend.__init__ constructs its own (self._embed = EmbedClient()) and hands it to scoring.rank() inside backend.search(); wiring rerank into the CLI needs a deliberate seam for the client (new backend method, or an EmbedClient built in the handler) rather than reaching into backend._embed
the EmbedClient seam is explicit and testable - a test injects a fake client through the seam without monkeypatching backend._embed, proving the handler does not reach into backend internals

EmbedClient.rerank() swallows every exception into _local_rerank, and the two lanes return numbers on the same 0..1 scale with entirely different meaning (live lane: 0.968 on-topic vs 3.2e-05 distractor; lexical fallback: 0.034 vs 0.016), so a caller cannot tell a degraded answer from a good one - the degradation must become visible at the call site
a test asserts the two lanes are distinguishable at the call site: given a raising remote lane, the caller can tell it got lexical numbers WITHOUT inspecting the score values themselves

the rerank stage is OPT-IN and default recall behaviour is byte-unchanged: --mode hybrid without --rerank keeps its current ordering, scores and bundle shape. Issue #3 (jetson-ai-lab-cli) and the research-flow consumers (#1) already absorbed one breaking bundle change in 0.13.0; a second silent reordering of the primary tier is not on the table
a golden-output test proves default recall is byte-unchanged: the same query with no --rerank produces an identical bundle (same items, same order, same scores) before and after this change

recall stays fetch-only: reranking is scoring a (query, stored-text) pair with a cross-encoder, not generating text. No item text is synthesised, rewritten or summarised anywhere on this path - the fetch-only guarantee stated in recall.py module docs and CLAUDE.md survives verbatim
grep proves it structurally: no LLM/completion/chat endpoint is reachable from the recall path, and every emitted item text is byte-identical to the stored record text

the freshness blend must not double-apply: scoring._blend_signal already multiplies score by (1 + 0.25*(signal-0.5)) inside rank(), uniformly across all four modes. Whatever rerank_score means, it must not be silently re-blended, and score must not be re-blended a second time after the rerank pass
a test pins the blend applies exactly once: a record with real temporal data has the same score under --rerank as without it, proving the rerank pass did not re-run _apply_blend

the test suite stays hermetic and offline: tests/test_scoring.py and tests/test_signal_strength.py deliberately construct EmbedClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:1/v1") so every ranking test exercises the local fallback with no server. Rerank tests follow that posture - fake/injected clients, never a live lane in CI
the full suite passes with no network route to the lobes gateway (run with the endpoint pointed at a dead port), proving no test depends on a live lane

docs/contract.md §5 embed_default_* block, tests/test_embed_default_drift.py and BOTH vendored wrappers (.claude/skills/{recall,remember}/scripts/*.sh) are locked together by a drift test. EIDETIC_RERANK_MODEL is already in all three. If the opt-in gains an env var with a wrapper-exported default, all three surfaces move together or CI fails
tests/test_embed_default_drift.py still passes unchanged, and if this change adds no env var the test file needs no edit at all - a diff on that file is itself the signal that c14 was triggered

the hand-maintained docs trio drifts if any one is missed - CLAUDE.md names it explicitly: eidetic/explain/catalog.py (the _RECALL verbatim doc, ~line 182-333), eidetic/cli/_commands/learn.py (_TEXT + _as_json_payload) and eidetic/cli/_commands/overview.py (_VERBS line 63). README.md line 40 and .claude/skills/recall/SKILL.md + recall.sh usage text carry the same flag list a fourth and fifth time

teken cli doctor . --strict stays green and every one of the five flag-listing surfaces (explain catalog _RECALL, learn, overview, README line 40, recall SKILL.md + recall.sh usage) names --rerank - verified by grepping for the flag across all five, not by eyeballing

the threshold and the fallback interact and must not be applied blindly: a relevance cutoff calibrated on cross-encoder scores (0.968 vs 3.2e-05) is meaningless against lexical-overlap scores (0.034 vs 0.016, same 0..1 scale). When the explicitly-permitted lexical fallback is in use, the threshold must either be skipped or be a separately-stated lexical cutoff - never the remote one reused

a test pins the interaction directly: with the fallback permitted and a raising remote lane, a record scoring below the REMOTE threshold on lexical overlap is NOT dropped - proving the remote cutoff was not reused on a lexical score

--rerank without the fallback opt-in FAILS CLOSED: an unreachable or unauthenticated lane raises CliError (exit 1/2 per the error contract, error: + hint: lines, no traceback) rather than answering with lexical numbers. Given the live probe (401 with no bearer token) this is the common misconfiguration, so the remediation line must name the API key variables by name

a test asserts the failure is closed and legible: an unreachable/401 lane with no fallback opt-in exits non-zero with an error: line and a hint: line naming EIDETIC_EMBED_API_KEY, and emits no bundle to stdout

when - and only when - a caller passes --rerank-threshold, recall can return FEWER than --top-k results, including zero. Every downstream stage keys off the surviving hits: a dropped record is not emitted in any tier, is not used as a traversal seed, and is not reinforced. With the post-challenge default (reorder only, c29) the hit count is unchanged from today

a test proves the drop propagates coherently: a record dropped by the threshold appears in no tier of the bundle, is not used as a traversal seed, and its recall_count/last_recall are unchanged in the store afterwards

ordering and score deliberately diverge under --rerank: items are ordered by rerank_score while score keeps its hybrid value, so a consumer re-sorting by score disagrees with the emitted order. This is what issue #39 asks for; the docs surfaces (catalog _RECALL, README, SKILL.md) must say so outright rather than leave it inferable

a test asserts the divergence explicitly: under --rerank the emitted item order differs from a descending sort on score, and the docs surfaces state this in words a consumer will read before assuming otherwise

every recall caller who has watched a relevant record sit below an irrelevant one: the jetson-ai-lab-cli consumer (#3) building cited answers, the research-flow agents (#1), the fanned-out /recall skill wrappers used by Claude and the colleague backend, and any agent whose top-k is padded with near-miss records hybrid scored at ~0.23
the issue #39 thread records that the named consumers were told - the opt-in flag means none of them must act, but they are told it exists

a caller who adds --rerank gets a bundle whose primary tier has been re-scored by the lobes cross-encoder: off-topic records that hybrid surfaced are dropped below the threshold rather than padding top-k, survivors are ordered by rerank_score with their hybrid score still visible beside it, and if the lane is unreachable or unauthenticated the call FAILS with a named remediation instead of quietly answering with lexical-overlap numbers

a live run against the real lobes gateway reproduces the after-state end to end: --rerank on a real store drops an injected distractor, keeps the on-topic records, and an unauthenticated run exits non-zero with the remediation line

EmbedClient.rerank() ships complete and is called by nothing; recall is embedding+BM25 only, with no rerank flag. Worse, the method is a trap for whoever wires it next: it swallows every exception into a lexical-overlap fallback that returns numbers on the same 0..1 scale, so a 401 from the gateway looks exactly like a working reranker
the before-state is verifiable in git history at the parent commit: grep shows rerank( called from nowhere outside embed.py and its tests, and recall has no rerank flag

the lane is now calibrated and measurably discriminating - on real eidetic records it kept the two on-topic ones at 0.993/0.936 and sent both off-topic records hybrid had surfaced at ~0.23 to 0.000 - so the recall tail is improvable today with code eidetic already owns. And the silent fallback is a correctness hazard independent of the feature: it is how eidetic#28 shipped an endpoint that always 401ed without anyone noticing for four months
the improvement is demonstrated, not asserted: the live run records before/after orderings for at least one real query, and the PR quotes both

an offline, hermetic test proves all three behaviours against an injected client: (1) with a fake remote lane scoring a distractor 0.0, --rerank drops it and reorders the survivors by rerank_score while score keeps its hybrid value; (2) with the lane raising, --rerank exits non-zero with error:/hint: naming the API key variables; (3) with the fallback explicitly permitted, the call succeeds, the payload marks the lexical lane and the remote-calibrated threshold is not applied to lexical scores
all three numbered behaviours exist as named, individually-failing tests - not one combined test that passes for the wrong reason - and each is mutation-verified by breaking the code it covers

a literal 0.0 threshold drops NOTHING: rerank scores are strictly positive and the issue table"s "0.000" is display rounding. Measured floors: 3.2e-05 for the "Cats purr" distractor in a 2-doc pool, but 1.6e-4 to 1.8e-4 for irrelevant docs in a 50-doc pool - the floor MOVES with pool size and composition, so the default must be a real number chosen against a pool of the configured size, not the literal zero the issue table suggests
a test asserts a 0.0 threshold is a no-op on strictly-positive scores, so nobody later mistakes it for drop-everything-irrelevant

the h4 round-trip test is VACUOUS as written: record_to_envelope (backend.py:264) is an explicit field WHITELIST that omits score and signal by construction, so rerank_score can never persist no matter what cmd_recall nulls. A test that stores and re-reads will pass identically on buggy code. It must use a stand-in that bypasses the whitelist, plus a control assertion that fails when the guard is removed - this is the THIRD occurrence of this trap in this repo (get_many pre-filtering in #37, data_refinery list() can_serve in #23)
the rerank_score non-persistence test is mutation-verified: it FAILS when the guard is deliberately removed, proving it is not passing on the envelope whitelist alone

the threshold turns _remote_rerank"s missing-index default into silent data loss: score_map.get(i, 0.0) maps any index the server omits or returns out of range to 0.0. As a ranking input that is benign; combined with --rerank-threshold it becomes a DROP, so a partial or malformed response makes records vanish with no error. A response shorter than the batch must be detected and raised rather than defaulted - this holds whenever the threshold is available, not only when it is on
a test feeds a response missing one index and asserts an error is raised, not a 0.0 score substituted

a --rerank-threshold that drops primary hits is a SILENT CUT, the exact thing #37 ruled out when it made truncated mandatory for a bound that cuts a walk short. When a caller opts into the threshold, the bundle must report how many primary hits it removed. Under the default (reorder only) nothing is cut and no marker is needed
with --rerank-threshold set, a test asserts the bundle reports the number of primary hits removed; without it, the payload is unchanged from today

CROSS-REPO COLLISION found by the adjacent-systems lens: colleague/memory.py already ships filter_recall_records(min_score, min_signal) with COLLEAGUE_RECALL_MIN_SCORE, thresholding recalled records on the score field before injection, and score_recall_precision ranks over the recalled ORDER. Under c23 (order by rerank_score, score keeps its hybrid value) colleague would threshold on hybrid scores while reading a rerank order - cutting exactly the records the reranker ranked first. Whatever field carries the authoritative relevance must be stated to that consumer, not left to be inferred
the field carrying authoritative relevance is stated explicitly in the bundle docs, and colleague is told on the issue thread that a score-based min_score filter no longer matches rerank order

rerank sends record TEXT to the gateway, so a --visibility private recall ships private record text over HTTP - pre-existing for embeddings (embed_detect already posts candidate texts) but AMPLIFIED here: the pool widens the batch from top-k (5) to 50, roughly a tenfold increase in private text leaving the process per call. This is the same exposure the borrowed-key withholding logic in embed.py already guards against, and it must be stated rather than inherited silently
the docs state that --rerank posts record text to the endpoint and that the pool sets the batch size, so a private-scope caller can see the exposure before opting in

tasks.instruction: This is a pure engine in the style of eidetic/memory/traverse.py and lifecycle.py - read one of them first for the house shape. No imports of store, backend, embed, or datetime. It receives already-computed scores and returns ordered records plus a dropped count. The two subtle cases are the whole point of the task: a 0.0 threshold must be a no-op on strictly-positive scores, and a remote-calibrated threshold must never be applied to lexical-lane scores.

risks.text: the other ~57 fanned-out consumers of recall output were never surveyed for the same score-thresholding collision colleague has (frame s23). If another one filters or re-sorts on score, --rerank ordering silently misleads it too - and this plan will not find that out

no eidetic-side evaluation set exists: every quality claim about --rerank rests on ad-hoc probes run by hand against two queries. t9 demonstrates the feature works, NOT that it improves recall across the real corpus - and nothing in this plan measures that

a caller who passes --rerank-threshold on an untemplated host (Thor/Orin, until their next `lobes init --apply`) can still lose relevant records, and eidetic cannot detect templated-vs-untemplated from the response shape. Mitigated to non-blocking only because thresholding is off by default
rerank latency was measured on an idle fleet (0.07s for 50 docs). Behaviour under concurrent load from other mesh agents is unmeasured, and recall sits on the hot path for agent context
